text:
liam_support: customer ACME reporting lots of 5xx and timeouts from hosted API in us-east-1 since 08:12 UTC. p95->p999 tail spiking, many requests hitting gateway timeout. queue depth jumped to ~11.2k.

samir_sre: on it. do you have a sample request or any correlation id? suspect continuous-batching backlog + dequeue slow.

liam_support: pasted sample curl and X-Request-Id from the customer: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" -d '{\"input\":\"longtext...\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` id: r-ACME-08:12:57-9a7f

opsbot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: hosted-gateway-high-queue-depth (alert-1234) — current queue_depth=11234, p95_latency=3.8s, p999_latency=12.1s

maria_eng: thanks. grabbing traces for r-ACME-08:12:57-9a7f. initial observation: requests are getting enqueued but not batched through for >8s. continuous-batcher backlog growing. KV cache misses also increased.

samir_sre: can you dump the batcher metrics? `kubectl -n runtime exec -it batcher-ctrl -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep batch`

maria_eng: `batch_queue_length{pool=\"hosted-us-east-1\"} 11234` and `batch_dequeue_rate 23 req/s` on the affected shard. dequeue_rate stuck low.

liam_support: customer says this coincided with a sudden burst of long-sequence requests (token ~12k). they were streaming but through single-shot generate calls.

jen_prod: any auth/billing errors? could token validation be adding latency?

maria_eng: auth latency normal (~20ms). no billing-related 429s. backend GPU workers are healthy but processors show high per-token CPU from longseq requests. Means longer per-request service time -> reduced throughput -> backlog.

samir_sre: probable causal chain: longseqs bump service time -> batcher gathers fewer requests per second -> queue depth increases -> tail latency skyrockets -> gateway times out. Need immediate mitigation to protect low-latency tenants.

liam_support: customer wants a mitigation now; they're seeing user-facing timeouts and 502/504s.

maria_eng: temporary mitigations we can run now: 1) enable tenant isolation for ACME to a dedicated warm pool, 2) lower continuous-batcher max_wait_ms from 200ms -> 50ms so we prioritize latency over throughput, 3) increase dequeue workers on shard, 4) enable model-fallback to a smaller quantized variant for longseqs.

samir_sre: ordering: quick wins first — reduce batch max_wait and scale batcher replicas. I can bump replicas and patch config.

jen_prod: Recommend also enabling request-shed for thinpool when queue_depth > 8k to protect critical tenants. Can we set a soft cap and automatic fallback?

maria_eng: yes, config patch: `continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=50`, `batcher.replicas += 2`, `ingress.soft_queue_cap=8000, ingress.fallback_policy=route-to-dedicated`. Applying now.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rolling patch applied to runtime-config us-east-1: continuous-batcher.max_wait_ms -> 50ms, batcher replicas +2 (patch-4857).

liam_support: after changes customer reports reduced 5xxs. p95 down to 420ms, p999 at ~2.1s. queue depth falling.

samir_sre: follow-up items: 1) add longseq detection to earlyroute so very long token requests go to dedicated longseq pool, 2) tune batcher to detect KV cache thrash, 3) add alerting for dequeue_rate drop.

maria_eng: opened ENG ticket #ENG-1298 for longseq earlyroute and batcher heuristics.

liam_support: customer asked for postmortem and config changes. I'll send them a short timeline and actions taken.

jen_prod: please include recommended guardrails for customers (max recommended tokens per hosted request, guidance to use streaming + chunking, and contact point to request dedicated capacity).

liam_support: will draft a message.

opsbot: Incident status -> mitigated. monitoring for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:

liam_support: thanks team. cc @maria_eng please add any logs I should include in customer note.
